_about: One edition of the app: its name, welcome page, quotes, colors and the voices
reflections draw on. The library of quotable works is sources.json in this folder,
and Claude's instructions are in prompts/. Choose the edition with the EDITION
description: A private journal, with a thoughtful reflection after every entry.
lead: A quiet place for a few honest lines a day, with a thoughtful reflection waiting after every entry.

points.title: A few honest lines are enough
points.text: One small, true thought counts; the benefit comes from reflecting each day. A prompt is there when the page feels blank.

points.title: A well-stocked library of wisdom
points.text: Reflections draw only on {works} chosen works, from Plato and the Stoics to Kierkegaard, and tell you exactly where to find each passage.

points.title: Explore past reflections with prompted questions
points.text: Every reflection ends with a question to carry forward. Browse back by date, or keep favorites close.

points.title: Private, and never used to train AI
points.text: Entries are encrypted with a passphrase only you know. Your entry only goes to Claude to write your daily reflection, and isn’t used to train it.

welcome_quote.text: “The unexamined life is not worth living.”

sources_intro: Reflections quote only the works below, each in a public-domain translation (or original English edition) on Wikisource. Every quotation is checked word for word against that text before you see it, and links to the passage it came from.

source_groups.name: Classical Greece
source_groups.about: Athens, from the 5th to the 3rd century BC, where the examined life began. Socrates wrote nothing; his words come to us through Plato's dialogues.

source_groups.name: Rome and the Stoics
source_groups.about: Cicero, and the Stoics Seneca, Epictetus and Marcus Aurelius: philosophy as a practice for living, in good fortune and bad.

source_groups.name: Late antiquity and the Middle Ages
source_groups.about: Faith and reason together: from Augustine and Boethius to Anselm, Aquinas and Dante.

source_groups.name: Early modern philosophy
source_groups.about: The 17th and 18th centuries: doubt, reason, the passions and the self.

source_groups.name: Modern philosophy
source_groups.about: Duty, freedom and the single individual: Kant, Kierkegaard and Mill.
